result:
Going ahead on the New-Project Entry. Below are the outcome candidates, taken from the spec's §3 Rulings and §2.1 scope. I haven't ranked them; that's your call.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome (what you get) | From | Cost note |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a range you choose, downloaded once with original bytes kept | R1, R6 | Unverified. Roughly 130 quarters since 1993, each master index tens of MB, so likely a few GB in total. Requests are negligible at 3 req/s; bandwidth dominates. The probe below would firm this up. |
| O2 | A canonical filing-index dataset (one row per filing, with provenance) built from those indexes | R3 | Measured by the core stage. Parse time per quarter is unknown until a real quarter runs. |
| O3 | Daily indexes added on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2 | About 250 small files a year. Size per file is measured by its stage. |
| O4 | Reprocessing stored bytes after a parser change, with no new SEC download | R6 | Compute only, bounded by O2's measured parse time. |
| O5 | Quarterly reconciliation: additions and field changes recorded, and closed-quarter withdrawals held for your hash-bound approval | R7, R10 | Your time per approval. The rate of withdrawals is unknown until it runs. |
| O6 | Readers always get a complete quarter generation through one active pointer, never partial files | R9 | Small. |
| O7 | All SEC traffic under one shared budget (3 req/s, one collector at a time), whatever runs concurrently | R8 | No dollar cost. It caps O1's wall time. |
| O8 | The whole thing running unattended on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor), with alerts and runbooks | R4, §4.7–4.9 | Azure spend can't be estimated without your region and pricing tier. It is measured by this track's first deployment. |
| O9 | Configuration (range, handoff date, SEC identity, limits) checked before any network request | R11, §4.8 | Small. |

## Proposed tracks

- **Track A: Filing-index catalog** (known progression): O1, O2, O3, O4, O5, O6, O7, O9. The spec names these stages in order.
- **Track B: Azure operation** (known progression): O8.
  - **Why split:** a correct catalog built and run locally stands without Azure, and the Azure deployment is a different use, unattended operation. Joined, the first usable catalog would wait on ADF, identities and infrastructure-as-code. B depends on A's commands existing, so it would come after at least A's core stage.

Under §7's rules, Track A's core stage would work on real data at the smallest usable standard. Basic User-Agent identification and throttling would be in it, since it talks to the SEC. The shared cross-collector lease (O7), the pointer (O6) and replay (O4) would be named later stages, not part of the core stage's exit.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), as a uv workspace.
- Azure as the platform (R4, the ADR). Both the spec and the ADR are still **PROPOSED**, so I'm treating Azure as a choice you've made pending acceptance. Tell me if it's still open.
- **Package layout.** The spec places all code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`, but the repo also has `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-index-ingest` scaffolds that the spec doesn't mention. I'll record whatever layout you confirm and leave the decision of where code goes to each stage.

## Proposed name

`sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec`, giving `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md` (the spec's stem, used whole).

## Optional probe

One read-only request for `Archives/edgar/full-index/index.json` and a few quarter listings, to replace O1's guess with real sizes. I'll run it only if you say yes.

---

**Please rank the outcomes within each track and the two tracks against each other, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds, the package-layout note and the name.**
